clue.text: Kitty turned awkward situation into means of escape!

indicators.note: something turned round faces the other way, so this word is read from its end back to its start

blocks.note: a kitty is a shared pool of money, as in a card game
to be in a hole is to be in a fix

explanation.surface: A cat backed into a tight spot somehow finds a way out.
explanation.walkthrough: Kitty looks like a cat but is the pot of money; reversed it sits in front of the hole.
explanation.definitionFit: A loophole is a gap in rules or law that lets someone evade an obligation, an escape route.

clue.text: Where the tablecloth might go on the other side

blocks.note: playfully, a cloth goes over the leaf, the hinged extension of a table
the usual sense: on the reverse of the page

explanation.walkthrough: A table leaf is the extra flap that extends it, so the cloth is laid over it; the word itself means 'see the back of this page'.
explanation.definitionFit: Printed instructions say continued overleaf when text runs on to the reverse of the sheet.

clue.text: Influence a racy individual to gain unfair advantage

blocks.note: pull is clout or influence, as in having pull with the boss
taken as written
fast describes someone racy or loose-living, and one is an individual

explanation.surface: Someone sways a fast-living character so as to get an edge over others.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to trick or cheat someone, getting the better of them by deceit.

clue.text: Astonished public observe Dutch leader

indicators.note: the leader of a word is whatever stands at its front, so only its initial is kept

blocks.note: something public is open to all
to eye something is to watch it
the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: The crowd stares in amazement at the prime minister of the Netherlands.
explanation.definitionFit: Wide-eyed with wonder: eyes opened wide in surprise or amazement.

clue.text: Learned what is said in France after game in Europe ends

indicators.note: coming after places the French phrase directly behind the game in the sequence
the ends of a word are its first and last characters, all else discarded
being in something means sitting inside it, so the outer pair wraps the rest

blocks.note: RU is rugby union
dit is French for said
the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: Someone learnt, at a match's close on the continent, what the French were saying.
explanation.walkthrough: Learned is read as the adjective (learn-ed), meaning scholarly, not the past tense of learn.
explanation.definitionFit: An erudite person has deep scholarly knowledge, which is what learned means as an adjective.

clue.text: Ornamental miniature box, say

blocks.note: the surface suggests a tiny decorative container or casket
box is an evergreen shrub, here an example of a dwarfed potted tree

explanation.walkthrough: Box looks like a container but is the shrub; the say marks it as one example of a tree kept tiny by the Japanese art.
explanation.definitionFit: The Japanese art produces deliberately dwarfed trees and shrubs grown in shallow pots for ornament; box is a favourite subject.

clue.text: Show extreme affection for wife in the cooler'

indicators.note: one thing sitting in another is held inside it, so the device wraps around the partner

blocks.note: W is the standard abbreviation for wife
a fan cools the air; the cooler is not prison here

explanation.surface: A husband gushes over his wife while she is locked up in jail.
explanation.walkthrough: The cooler is slang for prison, which is the false path; here it is the device that cools you.
explanation.definitionFit: To fawn is to flatter or show exaggerated fondness, like a dog fussing over its owner.

clue.text: Riotous repartee to watch, possibly

indicators.note: something riotous is wild and disorderly, so these letters are thrown out of order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Some uproarious witty banter is well worth tuning in to watch.
explanation.walkthrough: Watch is a timepiece, not a verb, and possibly flags it as one kind.
explanation.definitionFit: A repeater is a pocket watch that chimes the hours when a button is pressed, so it is one type of timepiece.

clue.text: One who shares opportunity with a friend

blocks.note: room is scope or opportunity, as in room for improvement
a mate is a friend

explanation.surface: Someone generous gives a chance to a pal.
explanation.definitionFit: A room-mate is a person sharing accommodation with another, so someone who shares living space.

clue.text: Trade alliance covering distribution

blocks.note: first meaning: a commercial agreement or bargain between parties
second meaning: the handing out of cards to players

explanation.surface: A commercial pact sets out how goods are to be shared out.
explanation.definitionFit: A deal is a business agreement, and also the dealing of cards round a table at the start of a hand.

clue.text: Sending a clot to make a call

definitions.note: the answer is an adjective describing such a call

indicators.note: to make something is to form it from raw material, so these letters are fashioned anew

blocks.note: every letter of these three words is used

explanation.surface: Someone dispatches an idiot to go and phone somebody.
explanation.walkthrough: Sending and clot both seem to carry meaning but are just letters; clot is British slang for a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: A trunk call made over a great distance, to another town or country, is described with this adjective.

clue.text: A contemporary record containing the facts admitted

indicators.note: something containing another holds it inside, so the record wraps the facts

blocks.note: taken as written
a compact disc, the modern kind of record in 1992
the facts known about something make up what is known

explanation.surface: A modern document holding the facts was conceded as true.
explanation.definitionFit: To acknowledge something is to admit or accept it as true, so admitted is the past participle.

clue.text: Take sides about female imprisoned by governor in the Tower

indicators.note: going about something means surrounding it, so the two sides flank the woman
a prisoner is held inside the walls, so the governor encloses the group

blocks.note: the two sides, left and right
F is the abbreviation for female
a bey was a governor in the Ottoman Empire

explanation.surface: A woman jailed in the Tower of London is forced to choose a faction.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tower suggests London's prison, but the definition is only a tower; bey is an old Turkish title for a provincial ruler.
explanation.definitionFit: A belfry is the tower or upper chamber of a church in which the bells hang.

clue.text: Choose judge with the right qualifications

blocks.note: to judge is to think or reckon
fit means suitable or qualified for a task

explanation.surface: A panel picks the magistrate who has the proper credentials.
explanation.walkthrough: Judge looks like a noun for the person chosen but is a verb, to reckon.
explanation.definitionFit: To think fit to do something is to decide or see proper to do it, so to choose.

clue.text: The driver's right in an illegal position

blocks.note: first meaning: the side of a British car nearer the middle of the road, where the driver sits
second meaning: in football or rugby, ahead of the ball where a player may not play it

explanation.surface: A motorist insists on the right of way while parked illegally.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain cars drive on the left, so the off side is the right-hand side, where the driver sits.
explanation.definitionFit: The off side of a vehicle is the side away from the kerb, and in sport a player ahead of play is caught out of position.

clue.text: Kindly doing a favour

blocks.note: first meaning: helpful and good-natured, as an adjective
second meaning: present participle of the verb, putting someone in your debt

explanation.definitionFit: Obliging is an adjective for someone willing to help, and also the verb form for rendering a service to someone.

clue.text: The Church is in a kind of eclipse, writes intellectual

indicators.note: being in something means lying inside it, so the eclipse wraps around the church

blocks.note: CH is the abbreviation for church
an eclipse of the sun is one kind

explanation.surface: A clever writer argues that religion has gone into a dark period.
explanation.definitionFit: A scholar is a learned academic person, one who lives by the intellect.

clue.text: Order regiment to Berlin, for instance

blocks.note: to compose is to arrange or put in order
R is an abbreviation for regiment

explanation.surface: A general sends troops off to the German capital.
explanation.walkthrough: Berlin is not the city but Irving Berlin, the American songwriter of White Christmas.
explanation.definitionFit: Irving Berlin wrote hundreds of popular songs, so he is an example of a writer of music.

clue.text: Prop for, perhaps, a vocal solo turn

blocks.note: an air is a tune, perhaps one sung by a single voice
to screw something is to turn it

explanation.surface: Something to lean on when a singer performs a solo spot.
explanation.walkthrough: Prop looks like a support but is short for propeller.
explanation.definitionFit: A prop is a propeller, the rotating blades that drive an aircraft, also called this word.

clue.text: Hothead abandoned the game, the ignorant fellow!

indicators.note: what is abandoned is left behind, so this letter walks out of the word

blocks.note: the head, or first letter, of the word hot
a game bird shot for sport

explanation.surface: A hot-tempered player storms off from the match, the oaf!
explanation.walkthrough: Hothead reads as a quick-tempered person; split, it is the head of hot. Peasant is used here, old-fashionedly, as an insult for a boor.
explanation.definitionFit: Peasant is used as a disparaging word for an uncouth, uneducated or boorish person.

clue.text: Only endless piety can create a facility for composition

indicators.note: with no end, the word loses its final letter
to create is to build something new, so the letters are rebuilt in a fresh order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, before its tail is dropped

explanation.surface: Pure unbroken devotion is what makes a place for writing music.
explanation.walkthrough: Composition sounds musical, but here it is typesetting, composing type.
explanation.definitionFit: The Linotype machine cast whole lines of metal type, a device newspapers used for composing text.

clue.text: An American would put this on runners

blocks.note: first meaning: slang for someone from the United States
second meaning: a punter's bet placed on horses in several races

explanation.walkthrough: Runners suggests sledge runners, but they are horses in races; in British betting this is a combination wager on four horses.
explanation.definitionFit: A Yank is an American, and the bookmaker's term names an accumulator bet of eleven wagers on four selections.

clue.text: Morals corrupted by champers?

indicators.note: something corrupted is spoilt from its proper form, so these letters are jumbled

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Is decency ruined by too much bubbly?
explanation.walkthrough: Champers is British slang for champagne, but here it means things that champ, or chew.
explanation.definitionFit: Molars are the back grinding teeth, the ones that champ and chew food.

clue.text: Promise to present unit with a weapon

blocks.note: to present is to give
one is the single unit
a sword is a bladed weapon

explanation.surface: A commander pledges to equip a military unit with arms.
explanation.walkthrough: The word is split differently in the answer: the last piece supplies both the possessive ending and the final word.
explanation.definitionFit: To give one's word is to make a solemn promise or pledge of honour.

clue.text: Exceedingly light

blocks.note: first meaning: to a high degree
second meaning: a coloured signal flare fired from a pistol

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as 'extremely light in weight', but light is a noun: a Very light is a signal flare, named after its inventor.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb intensifies like extremely, and Edward Very gave his name to a flare shot from a pistol.

clue.text: Clothing to boast about

indicators.note: turning about means facing the opposite way, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: to brag is to boast

explanation.surface: Fine clothes are something to show off about.
explanation.definitionFit: Garb is a word for dress or attire, especially distinctive costume.

clue.text: Territory controlled by Darwin from Scotland perhaps

definitions.note: the answer is the word naming this territory

blocks.note: first meaning: Darwin is the capital of Australia's ... Territory
second meaning: belonging to the north, as Scotland is of Britain

explanation.surface: A naturalist's domain is said to lie up in Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: Darwin suggests Charles Darwin, but it is the city in Australia.
explanation.definitionFit: Australia's Northern Territory is governed from Darwin, and Scottish things are northern from England's viewpoint.

clue.text: Decline to go round the county

blocks.note: to turn is to go round
County Down is in Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: A traveller refuses to make a circuit of the shire.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn down an offer is to refuse or reject it.
